faq.q: How far is Sotogrande from Puerto Banús by boat?
faq.a: The distance from Puerto Banús to Sotogrande is roughly 12 nautical miles. At a cruising speed of 20–25 knots, the trip takes about 30–40 minutes depending on sea conditions. This is far quicker than the road journey, which can take over an hour during polo final traffic.

faq.q: Can I anchor near the Sotogrande Polo Club?
faq.a: Yes, you can anchor offshore near the beaches of Sotogrande, but the polo club itself is inland. Most boaters anchor off Playa de Sotogrande or Cala del Faro, then take a short tender or walk to the club. Your skipper can advise on the best spot on the day.

faq.q: Which boats are available for the Sotogrande Polo Final?
faq.a: We offer a range of boats departing from Puerto Banús. For a day out, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) and Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) are ideal, priced at €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours. For a larger group, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) is available from €4,719 for 4 hours, including a jet ski.

faq.q: What's included in the charter price?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). There are no hidden costs – the price you see is the price you pay.

faq.q: How far in advance should I book for the polo final?
faq.a: We recommend booking at least 2–3 weeks in advance for the Sotogrande Polo Final. The event attracts large crowds, and our boats are often fully booked the week before. Contact us via WhatsApp for the latest availability on your preferred date.

faq.q: Can I bring my own food and drinks on board?
faq.a: Yes, you're welcome to bring additional food and drinks. However, we already provide a selection of beverages and snacks. If you have specific preferences or dietary requirements, let us know in advance and we'll do our best to accommodate.

faq.q: What happens if the weather is bad on the day?
faq.a: Your safety is our priority. If the skipper deems conditions unsafe, we'll reschedule your charter to another day or offer a full refund. We monitor weather forecasts closely and will inform you as early as possible if any changes are needed.

data.body_html:
The Sotogrande Polo Final 2043 is more than a match – it's a full day of glamour, champagne, and high-octane sport. But getting there by road can be a nightmare: the A-7 clogs up, parking is scarce, and you'll miss half the atmosphere. The smarter move? Rent a boat from Puerto Banús and cruise the Costa del Sol in style. This guide covers everything you need to know about arriving by sea, from boat options to anchoring spots.

Why Arrive by Boat to the Sotogrande Polo Final?

Driving to Sotogrande on polo final day means gridlock. The roads around the club grind to a halt, and finding a parking spot can take an hour. By boat, you skip all that. Departing from Puerto Banús, you'll be at Sotogrande in 30–40 minutes, with the wind in your hair and a cold drink in hand. Plus, you get to enjoy the stunning coastline – La Concha looming behind Marbella, the golden sands of Cabopino, and the cliffs of Cala del Faro.

Which Boat to Choose for the Polo Final

We have a fleet of boats departing from Puerto Banús, each suited to different group sizes and budgets. Here are the top picks for the polo final:

  • Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) – perfect for a small group of friends. €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours.
  • Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) – a bit more space, same price point as the Astondoa.
  • Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) – the showstopper. €4,719 for 4 hours, with a jet ski thrown in free. Ideal if you want to make an entrance.
  • Other options – from the Pershing 46 (14m, 10 pax) to the Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax), we have boats for every taste. For pricing on these, message us on WhatsApp.

All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and IVA. No hidden extras.

Anchoring Near Sotogrande: Best Spots

Once you're near Sotogrande, your skipper will find the best anchorage. The most popular spots are Playa de Sotogrande and Cala del Faro. Playa de Sotogrande offers easy access to the club – a short tender ride or a walk along the beach. Cala del Faro is more secluded, with crystal-clear water for a pre-match swim. Remember, the polo club is inland, so you'll need to get to shore. Your skipper can help arrange a tender if needed.

What to Expect on Board

Your charter includes everything you need for a comfortable day: water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava, plus light snacks. If you want something more substantial, you're welcome to bring your own picnic – just let us know. The boats are equipped with shaded decks, sunbathing areas, and music systems. Some, like the Mangusta 80, have extra luxuries like a jet ski for a bit of fun before the match.

Timing Your Departure

The polo final typically starts in the late afternoon, but the party begins much earlier. We recommend departing Puerto Banús around 11:00–12:00. That gives you time to cruise, anchor, swim, and enjoy a leisurely lunch on board before heading ashore. After the match, you can stay for the celebrations or head back for a sunset cruise – the choice is yours. For an 8-hour charter, you'll have plenty of time to do both.

Pricing and Booking

Here's a quick reference for our most popular polo final charters:

Beyond the Polo: Exploring the Coast

If you're chartering for the whole day, make the most of it. After the match, cruise back towards Marbella and stop at Cala Cortés or Río Verde for a swim. Or head further west to Estepona and Sotogrande's marina for dinner. With an 8-hour charter, you can pack in a full day of exploration – from the glamour of Puerto Banús to the quiet coves of the Costa del Sol.
